security_audit.summary: Seven detections are documentation false positives: Markdown backticks, promotional links, permission checks, and an unrelated reconnaissance match. The privileged Apache stop-and-disable recommendation can disrupt services, although the guide presents it as a manual fix. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection; this package contains a guide, not executable diagnostic tooling.

remediation.issue: The example recommends stopping and persistently disabling Apache without checking dependent services or obtaining explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require dependency checks and explicit operator approval before service changes; prefer a reversible port adjustment and explain recovery before suggesting persistent disablement.

content.value_statement: Self-hosted service failures can involve conflicting ports, configuration errors, and permission problems. This guide structures agent-assisted diagnosis and manual repair recommendations for common Linux services.
actual_capabilities: Outlines checks for port conflicts between Docker containers and host services.
Identifies Nginx syntax errors and default_server collisions as diagnostic targets.
Covers Cloudflare Tunnel configuration and credential path troubleshooting.
Directs attention to systemd health, journald errors, and disk space exhaustion.
Includes PostgreSQL authentication and sensitive-file permission checks in the diagnostic scope.
Provides a worked example linking an Nginx startup failure to Apache occupying port 80.
limitations: Only the public guide is included; the original scripts, extension source, templates, and diagnostic engine are absent.
The guide targets Linux and lists Python 3 and local shell access as requirements.
Docker container internal networking audits are explicitly unsupported.
Repairs are manual; read-only behavior is described but not enforced by bundled executable tooling.

use_cases.title: Resolve a home lab port conflict
use_cases.description: Use the guide to compare host listeners and container port assignments when a new service fails to start.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Linux service outage
use_cases.description: Organize systemd, journald, disk space, and Nginx checks before proposing a manually reviewed repair.

use_cases.title: Review a self-hosted application deployment
use_cases.description: Check Cloudflare Tunnel paths, PostgreSQL authentication symptoms, and environment-file permissions using redacted evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a startup failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this guide to interpret my redacted Nginx startup error. Explain likely causes and request missing evidence. Do not run commands or change services.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner diagnosis from an error message

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a port conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my redacted listening-socket and Docker port listings. Identify conflicts and propose read-only checks. Do not stop services or alter configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Review tunnel and database symptoms
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my redacted Cloudflare Tunnel and PostgreSQL errors. Check path and permission hypotheses. Request metadata only; do not request secrets or modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan production triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan read-only triage across systemd, Nginx, sockets, disk usage, and permissions. Separate evidence from hypotheses. Include dependency checks, approval gates, and reversible repair options.

output_examples.input: Nginx fails to start. My supplied listener listing shows Apache using port 80.
output: Likely cause: Apache already occupies the port required by Nginx.
Next check: confirm the Nginx listen configuration and identify applications that depend on Apache.
Repair options: assign distinct ports or approve a service change after dependency review. No changes performed.

output_examples.input: Cloudflare Tunnel reports a missing credential file after I moved its configuration.
output: Possible cause: the configured credential path no longer matches the file location.
Next check: compare the configured path with file existence and service-user permissions.
Share only redacted paths and permission metadata. Do not provide credential contents.

best_practices: Start with redacted logs, socket listings, and permission metadata; keep credentials and environment values private.
Confirm service dependencies before considering port changes, service stops, or startup disablement.
Keep diagnosis read-only and require explicit approval plus a recovery plan for every proposed repair.
anti_patterns: Treating the public guide as an installed diagnostic engine or guaranteed automated scanner.
Executing the Apache stop-and-disable example without checking dependencies and obtaining approval.
Sharing complete environment files, tunnel credentials, or unredacted authentication logs.

faq.question: Does this package include the diagnostic engine?
faq.answer: No. The supplied file is a public guide. It explicitly excludes original scripts, extension source, and templates.

faq.question: Does it automatically repair my server?
faq.answer: No. The guide describes read-only diagnosis and manual repairs. Any agent actions depend on available tools, permissions, and your approval.

faq.question: Which systems and services does the guide cover?
faq.answer: It targets Linux, including Raspberry Pi environments, and covers Nginx, Cloudflare Tunnels, systemd, PostgreSQL, sockets, disk usage, and permissions.

faq.question: Can it diagnose Docker internal networking?
faq.answer: No. The guide explicitly excludes container internal networking audits, although it discusses port conflicts between containers and host services.

faq.question: Should I share environment files or tunnel credentials?
faq.answer: No. Share redacted errors and permission metadata. The described permission checks do not require secret values.

faq.question: What access is needed for diagnosis?
faq.answer: The guide lists Python 3 and local shell access. Initial review can use redacted logs; approve any local inspection separately.
